scope: Corollary 6.4 (Removing one factor while retaining the others) of the manuscript “Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers” (preprints/Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-in-the-positive-integers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 164 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ab835f6a98c10d6d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 45. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In Proposition 6.3, let q be another positive integer, fixed while t varies but permitted to change with w. Let a ∈ {0, . . . , q − 1}d also be independent of t. Suppose the spatial boxes have common scale Z0, with Z0/q dominating every fixed power of S. Suppose log Pt(a + qy) is polynomial jointly in (t, y) with fixed degree bound, and the normalized boxes lie in fixed multiples of [−Z0/q, Z0/q]d with comparable sides. Then, outside an exceptional proportion tending to zero, averaging Pt over the class a + qZd agrees to any prescribed accuracy with averaging over any compatible class modulo qt, with the same uniformities in boxes and tests. No coprimality between q and t is assumed.
